question.text: Under Sections 72 and 74 of the ITA, what are the carry-forward periods for (i) non-speculative business loss and (ii) capital loss?

answer.text: Both 8 years but inter-head set-off allowed indefinitely
(i) 8 years (business loss) — can only be set off against business income; (ii) 8 years (capital loss) — can only be set off against capital gains (LTCL only against LTCG, STCL against both)
(i) 4 years speculative and 8 years non-speculative; (ii) indefinite capital

explanation.text: The Logic: Section 72: non-speculative business loss carries forward 8 years; can be set off ONLY against business income (no inter-head carry-forward). Speculative business loss — 4 years (Section 73). Section 74: capital loss carries forward 8 years; can be set off ONLY against capital gains — LTCL only against LTCG, STCL against either STCG or LTCG. Intra-head rules apply first, then inter-head subject to restrictions. The Trap: Option A is the speculative rule only. Option B is half right — but missing the same-head restriction. Option D fabricates 'indefinite' carry-forward. Cross-Exam Context: X-A/B, XV, XXI-B all test this; XIX-C tests the pass-through of loss to unit-holders requiring 12-month minimum unit holding. Manager's Pro-Tip: Section 115UB: loss other than business loss passes through to unit-holders ONLY if they held units for at least 12 months at the time of set-off. Signal this in the PPM — early redeemers lose pass-through of losses.
